## Personality

Thoughtful, bookish and a little anxious. He knows the manual by heart and his arms do not.

## Lore

Tobe is seventeen, a recruit of the Royal Guard, and he knows the Court's sword manual by heart, every stance, every cut and every footnote. His arms do not. He read every book on swordsmanship in the Scholars' Quarter before he came to the Knights' Court, and he will tell anyone who asks that not one of them mentioned how heavy swords are. He is thoughtful, bookish and a little anxious, and he is still stuck on the third cut.

### The bindery boy

He grew up in the Scholars' Quarter with his elder sister Mariota, in two rooms over their father's bindery. Ranulf bound books for the Academy and the libraries, and the house was always full of them, and while Mariota read the histories, Tobe read the manuals: fencing, drill, the old treatises on the sword written by masters nobody remembers. Their mother, Sabine, died when he was five. Their father died two winters ago, and the bindery was sold to pay what was owed on it. Mariota had her place at the Academy. Tobe found work fetching and shelving books in a library in the Quarter, and in the long evenings between shelves he read, as far as he can tell, every book on the sword that has ever been bound in Selsior.

He read about the ranks of the Guard, from the Swordsman to the Grand Swordmaster, and about the one the old books name beyond them, the Sword Saint. He has read six different accounts of what a Sword Saint is, and they disagree about nearly everything, which bothers him more than it bothers anyone else. This spring, at seventeen, he closed the last book, put on his only good coat and walked to the Knights' Court to try the trials, on the theory that he already knew everything except how to do it.

### Step, strike

The theory was mostly correct, and that was the problem. Tobe can tell you exactly where his feet should be on the third cut, at what angle the blade should leave the guard and why. Then he tries it, and the sword goes somewhere else. Drill Sergeant Bertrand, who swears he can turn anyone into a guard given a year and enough porridge, bellows at him every morning, and Tobe mouths along with the corrections under his breath, because he has read them already, and it does not help. He drills alone in the evenings, step, strike, step, strike, counting under his breath. Captain Rhys watches sometimes and says nothing, which Tobe finds far worse than shouting.

His best friend is Pim, who salutes everyone and whose guard is full of holes. They share a bench at supper and a great deal of porridge, and they have a working arrangement: Tobe tells Pim exactly what he is doing wrong, and Pim makes Tobe laugh when the third cut goes wrong again. It works better than either of them expected. Pim says Tobe is the cleverest person in the Court. Tobe says Pim is the bravest, and has privately decided that brave is the more useful of the two with a sword in your hand.

Avice, the fiercest of their year, frightens him a little. She once watched him miss the third cut four times and then told him, in five words, what he was doing wrong. She was right. He has not yet worked out how to thank her.

### Mariota

His sister visits every week to ask whether he has got past the third cut yet, and to tease him for reading about swords instead of using them. He teases her back for reading about stars instead of looking at them. They are all the family either of them has, and they both know it, and neither of them says it.

### What he wants and fears

Tobe wants to earn the Swordsman's rank and to prove that a person who learned from books can learn from bruises too. He fears that he is the kind of person who will always know the answer and never be able to do it, and that one day, on a road somewhere, knowing the answer will not be enough.

### Hooks

A quest might begin with Tobe asking a passing adventurer to show him the third cut, slowly, because the books all describe it differently. Or it might begin with a seventh account of the Sword Saint, in a book Tobe has never seen, turning up on a stall in the Crown Market.
